relevance_note: Single case report of an infant with ATS and an SLC2A10 variant: "confirmed as ATS by postnatal genetic testing with a novel homozygous variant in SLC2A10 gene detected".
method_note: Hand-built from a full reading of the paper (no tables in the paper; a short script assembled the JSON and checked every span verbatim). The variant string contains non-breaking spaces as printed (c.173 C > T). In scope: the proband ('patient', rule 5) and both parents, who were tested and found to be carriers. One parent is labelled 'mother of patient' because the paper describes the mother ('A 28-year-old gravida 2 para 1 mother'); the other parent is never named by sex, so 'parent of patient' (no guessed 'father'). Parents' zygosity left 'not reported' because the paper says only 'carriers', not heterozygous. Proband inheritance recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' because the enum has no 'both parents' value; the statement is that both parents carry the same variant. The maternal aunt with an 'unknown genetic disease' is not in scope (no SLC2A10 variant or ATS diagnosis stated) and has no row. Age at onset recorded as the gestational age at first detection (21 weeks of gestation) with ISO null because it is a gestational, not postnatal, age; age at diagnosis left not reported because the prenatal diagnosis was of arterial tortuosity and the age at the genetic confirmation is not given. The mother's age (28 years) is at referral and is placed in age_at_last_evaluation. 'No coarctation' and 'no clinically significant stenoses requiring stenting or surgical intervention' were treated as narrower than the checklist item 'stenosis of the aorta or aortic branches', which stays not reported. Transient tachypnea of the newborn needing brief CPAP was mapped to the checklist item 'respiratory distress or insufficiency' as observed. Discussion statements about risks in ATS patients in general (pulmonary hypertension, hernias, scoliosis etc.) are not evidence about this patient. Severe preeclampsia is recorded as the mother's feature. No contradictions found.
